text: You step onto an escalator, just trying to get from A to B. It's moving, but you want to save those precious seconds.
Then you see it: people standing still on the right, a clear path opening on the left for those in a hurry. It’s an unspoken rule, universally understood.
You look for a sign, any official instruction. But there's nothing. No one told you to stand right, yet everyone simply... does.
This isn't a top-down command; it's an emergent system. When one person walks, others quickly realize it's more efficient if everyone keeps one side clear. It optimizes flow.
The cost? Breaking this unwritten rule creates friction. You block the path, slow others, and the system becomes less efficient for everyone. It’s subtle pressure.
So next time on the escalator, you'll see more than just steps. You'll recognize an invisible, self-organizing traffic system, designed to get us all there faster.
